title: Beatrix and the Orchard
premise: In 1911, Marguerite Thornbury, daughter of a pearl diver and indentured to the Meridian Trading Company in a colonial port, has learned that history is something that happens to other people. When an infant is abandoned at her door with a note instructing her to forget its face, she discovers the child is evidence of a massacre the company's allies intend to erase before the armistice negotiations conclude. Racing against the victors' historians who are already writing the official record, Marguerite gathers testimony from divers, clerks, and survivors, falling in love with a company archivist torn between duty and conscience. The book ends at the signing table: their record enters the proceedings too late to stop the armistice but early enough to be entered as a dissenting annex, preserving the truth—and giving the child, whom Marguerite keeps and names, a documented history after all.
about_author: Emrys Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading ledgers across three continents. They write historical fiction that recovers the voices ledger-keepers were paid to omit.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She dives for stray pearls to pay down her indenture, watching ships carry history away to elsewhere. Establishes her belief that events happen to other people. Emotional beat: resigned detachment masking grief for her drowned father.

chapters.title: Indenture Papers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The company clerk renews her contract with cold arithmetic; she memorizes the ledger room's layout out of habit. Introduces the port's hierarchy. Emotional beat: quiet resentment sharpening into curiosity about what the ledgers hide.

chapters.title: A Bundle at the Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A crying infant appears on her step with a note: forget this face. No mother, no name, only a company wax seal half-melted. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness colliding as she takes the child inside.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Elias Vane's POV. Company archivist Elias notices a missing file from the coastal registry and begins tracing it. He meets Marguerite when she comes asking innocent questions. Emotional beat: professional suspicion softening into fascination.

chapters.title: Milk and Ledgers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marguerite hides the baby among laundry while Elias audits her quarters; they circle each other with half-truths. Emotional beat: the first spark of alliance—two people lying well enough to trust each other.

chapters.title: The Face Worth Forgetting
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. An old diver recognizes the infant's features as belonging to a family from the burned village of Kessel Bay. Emotional beat: dread—the child isn't just abandoned; the child is a witness.

chapters.title: Kessel Bay Burns Twice
chapters.summary: Survivor Tomas Reyes' POV. Flashback chapter: the raid on Kessel Bay, ordered by company allies, and the second burning—of records, not houses. Emotional beat: trauma rendered as testimony, the past insisting on itself.

chapters.title: Duty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Elias' POV. His superior orders him to certify the falsified Kessel Bay registry. He complies, then copies the original by lamplight. Emotional beat: shame; the first crack in his loyalty.

chapters.title: The Historians Arrive
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A delegation of official historians lands to write the peace settlement's account. She watches them measure the town like appraisers. Emotional beat: realization that memory is now a race.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wound
chapters.summary: Tomas' POV. Tomas agrees to testify but warns Marguerite that witnesses have short lifespans here. Emotional beat: fear accepted as the price of truth.

chapters.title: What the Divers Saw
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Underwater, divers describe what sank off Kessel Bay: crates of confiscated documents dumped in the shallows. Emotional beat: hope surfacing like breath.

chapters.title: The Dive
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She dives the wreck site herself, retrieving a waterlogged dispatch naming the raid's author. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into danger—she was seen.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Elias' POV. The company offers Elias promotion and passage home if he delivers the missing dispatch. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare; love against duty takes its first true form.

chapters.title: The Baby's Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She names the child Aurelia and lets herself imagine a future beyond the indenture. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Registry
chapters.summary: Tomas' POV. A fellow witness sells information to the historians' fixers; one diver disappears overnight. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening around the small circle of truth-tellers.

chapters.title: The Armistice Clock
chapters.summary: Elias' POV. He learns the treaty will be signed in nineteen days; anything not on the record by then never happened. Emotional beat: urgency becomes the story's heartbeat.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Courtesy
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A polite historian interviews her over tea, probing about 'a certain infant.' She lies beautifully. Emotional beat: defiance dressed as deference.

chapters.title: Elias Chooses
chapters.summary: Elias' POV. He burns his promotion letter and brings the certified-false registry to Marguerite instead. Emotional beat: surrender—not to love, but to conscience.

chapters.title: The Testimony Circle
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Divers, clerks, and survivors gather in the drying loft to give sworn statements. Emotional beat: fragile community forming around paper and candlelight.

chapters.title: Raid on the Loft
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Soldiers seize the loft; statements scatter; Tomas is taken. Marguerite escapes with Aurelia and the dispatch hidden in pearl sacks. Emotional beat: loss and flight.

chapters.title: Prison Visit
chapters.summary: Elias' POV. He visits Tomas under pretext of inventory, receiving a memorized deposition because paper can be seized but memory must be killed. Emotional beat: courage without comfort.

chapters.title: The Historian Who Hesitates
chapters.summary: Historian Adela Crane's POV. One official historian privately doubts the record she's compiling; Marguerite gambles on approaching her. Emotional beat: cautious, dangerous sympathy.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A typhoon closes the port, freezing the treaty timetable and hiding the fugitives—but also threatening the sunken evidence. Emotional beat: nature as reluctant ally.

chapters.title: What the Storm Returned
chapters.summary: Tomas' POV (escaped). The storm washes crates ashore; villagers find more documents, including orders signed above the company. Emotional beat: vindication arriving battered but real.

chapters.title: Adela's Doubt
chapters.summary: Adela's POV. She compares the annex drafts with the salvaged originals and confronts her own complicity. Emotional beat: an institutional man's—or woman's—awakening.

chapters.title: The Price of Aurelia
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Fixers trace the baby; a friend shelters them at brutal cost. Marguerite must decide whether truth is worth orphaning Aurelia's safety. Emotional beat: maternal love tested against principle.

chapters.title: Double Entry
chapters.summary: Elias' POV. He forges audit trails to move the true registry into the official archive undetected. Emotional beat: the archivist finally weaponizes his duty.

chapters.title: The Informant's Face
chapters.summary: Tomas' POV. The betrayer is found—not punished, but recruited, offering the location of the final signature page draft. Emotional beat: mercy as strategy.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Become Three
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Negotiations accelerate; the signing moves up. The circle races to compile the annex. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into resolve.

chapters.title: The Vault
chapters.summary: Elias' POV. He breaks into the company vault at night to place the annex beside the treaty text. Alarms, near capture, Adela's unexpected cover. Emotional beat: climax of nerve.

chapters.title: Caught Between Covers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Elias is detained; Marguerite carries the last sworn statement to Adela directly, Aurelia in her arms as living evidence. Emotional beat: the personal made irrefutably political.

chapters.title: The Signing Table
chapters.summary: Adela's POV. Delegates sign the armistice; Adela moves to enter the dissenting annex. Objection, argument, a razor-thin procedural victory. Emotional beat: triumph that tastes like compromise.

chapters.title: Too Late to Stop It
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The armistice stands; the guilty walk free under amnesty. But the annex exists—on the record forever. Emotional beat: grief and grim satisfaction entwined.

chapters.title: Elias Released
chapters.summary: Elias' POV. Dismissed but unprosecuted, Elias chooses exile in the port over passage home. Emotional beat: belonging finally chosen over career.

chapters.title: Reading the Annex Aloud
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. In the drying loft, the community hears the annex read publicly for the first time; survivors weep at their own names in print. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into memorial.

chapters.title: Indenture Burned
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Amnesty chaos voids her contract papers; she is, technically and utterly, free—and unsure what freedom holds. Emotional beat: liberation as vertigo.

chapters.title: A History for Aurelia
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She writes Aurelia's origin into the annex margins so the child will one day know her own face was never meant to be forgotten. Emotional beat: memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Orchard
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On a hillside above the port, they plant an orchard—one tree for each Kessel Bay family, fruiting where the village stood. Emotional beat: rootedness after uprooting.

chapters.title: Victors' Historians, Revised
chapters.summary: Adela's POV. Years later, Adela publishes using the annex as primary source; the official story begins to crack. Emotional beat: slow justice, patiently believed.

chapters.title: Faces Remembered
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, closing. Aurelia, now a girl, asks about her face; Marguerite tells her everything, on the record and off. Emotional beat: peace—history no longer happens to other people.
